chunks: I heard ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrating to al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and he said: “By Allah, Allah certainly granted victory to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.” So al-Ḥasan said to him: “Yes, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you, his brothers surely transgressed against him.” So ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar said: “Yes, by Allah, and we, his paternal uncles, transgressed against him.”

So al-Ḥasan said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, what did you do? For I was not present with you.” He said: “His brothers said to him, and we as well: ‘There has never been among us an Imam of altered complexion.’ So al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to them: ‘He is my son.’ They said: ‘The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله judged by al-qāfah, so between us and you is al-qāfah.’ He said: ‘You send to them yourselves. As for me, no. And do not inform them why you invited them, and let yourselves remain in your houses.’”

So when they came, they seated us in the orchard, and his paternal uncles, his brothers, and his sisters lined up. They took al-Riḍā عليه السلام, clothed him in a woolen robe and a cap of it, placed a spade on his neck, and said to him: ‘Enter the orchard as though you are working in it.’ Then they brought Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and said: ‘Attach this boy to his father.’ They said: ‘He has no father here, but this is his father’s uncle, and this is his father’s uncle, and this is his uncle, and this is his paternal aunt. But if he has a father here, then he is the owner of the orchard, for his feet and his feet are one.’ So when Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام returned, they said: ‘This is his father.’

ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar said: “So I stood up and sucked the saliva of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, then I said to him: ‘I bear witness that you are my Imam before Allah.’ Then al-Riḍā عليه السلام wept and said: ‘O uncle, did you not hear my father while he was saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “May my father be for the son of the best of the slave-women, the son of the Nubian woman, pure of mouth, select of womb. Woe to them! May Allah curse al-Uʿaybis and his offspring, the possessor of tribulation. He will kill them for years and months and days, impose abasement upon them, and give them to drink a goblet that causes endurance. And he is the outcast, the fugitive, the one bereaved through his father and his grandfather, the possessor of the ghaybah, about whom it will be said: He died or he perished; in which valley did he travel?” O uncle, can this be anyone but me?’ So I said: ‘You have spoken the truth, may I be sacrificed for you.’”

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, identified here as the son of al-Riḍā عليه السلام
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: Imam; the divinely designated religious authority being discussed in the narration
key_terms.الشَّرِيدُ: the fugitive or displaced one; part of the description of the Imam in trial
key_terms.الطَّرِيدُ: the outcast; a description in the reported prophetic wording
key_terms.الْبُسْتَانِ: the orchard where the test of resemblance was arranged
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: the ghaybah; the occultation mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةِ: tribulation or strife associated with the persecuting force mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْقَافَةُ: physiognomic identification used here to determine family resemblance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the recognition of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and the prophetic indication of the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how the paternity of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was publicly confirmed in response to objections raised by some of Imam al-Riḍā’s عليه السلام relatives. It then moves from that episode to a declaration of his Imamate and a prophetic tradition indicating the lineage, trials, and ghaybah of a later Imam, highlighting continuity of divine designation within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, altogether from Zakariyya Bin Yahya Bin Al Nu’man Al Sayrafi who said, 
‘I heard Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> narrating to Al-Hassan Bin Al-Husayn Bin Ali Bin Al-Husayn, so he said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Granted victory to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>’. So Al-Hassan said to him, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, may I be sacrificed for you! His<sup>asws</sup> brothers had rebelled against him<sup>asws</sup>’. So Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, we, his<sup>asws</sup> uncles, had (also) rebelled against him<sup>asws</sup>’.

So Al-Hassan said to him, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! How did you behave, for I was not present with you all’. He said, ‘His<sup>asws</sup> brothers said to him<sup>asws</sup>, and us as well, ‘There has not been among us an Imam<sup>asws</sup> at all of a dark complexion’. So Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> is my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>!’. So they said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had judged (characters) based on appearance, therefore between us and you<sup>asws</sup> is the appearance’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You can send for them (experts in physiology), but as for I<sup>asws</sup>, so no, and do not let them know what you are inviting them for, and let them happen to be in your houses’.

So when they came, we got them to be seated in the orchard, and chose his<sup>asws</sup> uncles, and his<sup>asws</sup> brothers, and his<sup>asws</sup> sisters, and they took Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> and clothed him<sup>asws</sup> in a woollen robe and a skull cap and placed a spade upon his neck, and they said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Enter the orchard as if you<sup>asws</sup> are working in it’. Then they came with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and they said (to the experts in physiology), ‘Link this boy to his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>’. So they said, ‘There isn’t a father for him<sup>asws</sup> over here, but, this here is an uncle of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, and this one is an uncle of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, and this is his<sup>asws</sup> uncle, and this here is his<sup>asws</sup> paternal aunt, and if there was a father of his<sup>asws</sup> over here, so he<sup>asws</sup> is the one in the orchard, for his<sup>asws</sup> feet and his<sup>asws</sup> feet are one’. So when Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> returned, they said, ‘This is his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>!’

Ali Bin Ja’far said, ‘So I stood and I extracted the saliva of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, then I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I testify that you<sup>asws</sup> are my Imam<sup>asws</sup> in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> wept, then said: ‘O Uncle! Why did you not listen to my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘May my<sup>saww</sup> father<sup>as</sup> be for the son of the best of the slave girls of the sons of Nubia (Sudan), the aromatic of the mouth, the excellent of the womb!’. 
Woe be unto them! May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse the Abbasides and their offspring, the owners of the strife who have killed them (Imams<sup>asws</sup>) for years and months and days. They poisoned them<sup>asws</sup> and made them<sup>asws</sup> sick by sealed goblets, and he<sup>asws</sup> would be in exile, homeless, suffering the pain of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> grandfather. 
(as for) the Occultation, it would be said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> died, or perished’. (No one will know) which valley he<sup>asws</sup> would be travelling in. O Uncle! Can this happen to be except from me<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> speak the truth, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn al-Nu‘man al-Sayrafi who has said the following. “I heard Ali ibn Ja‘far speaking to al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn as, “By Allah, Allah has supported abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.).” Al-Hassan then said, “Yes, by Allah, may Allah take my souls in service for your cause, his brothers have rebelled against him.” Ali ibn Ja‘far then said, “Yes, by Allah, and we, his uncles, rebelled against him.”

Al-Hassan said to him, “May Allah take my souls in service for your cause, how did you dealt it, I was not present with you.” He said, “His brothers said to him and so did we, “there has never been a blackish Imam from us” The Imam (a.s.) al-Rida said to them, “He is my son.” They said,” Messenger of Allah did judge on the basis of physiognomy , thus, we can also have a judgment on the basis of physiognomy .” The Imam (a.s.) said, “You may call one who has said the following knows physiognomy but I will not do so. You should not give information as to for what reason you have called them. You must stay home.

When they will come, we should, all of us, be in the garden. His uncles, brothers and sisters should all line up. They dressed al-Rida (a.s.) in a gown made of wool with a hat of wool on his head and a shovel in his hand. The Imam should be asked to act as the gardener in the garden. Then abu Ja‘far should be brought in and they should be asked to find his father in the people present. They said, “His father is not present among these people, but this is his uncle, this is the uncle of his father, this is his uncle and this is his aunt. If his father is here he is the gardener because his foot print and his foot print matCh” When abu al-Hassan (a.s.) returned, they said, “This is his father.”

Ali ibn Ja‘far has said, “I stood up and kissed abu Ja‘far and his saliva came in my mouth. Then I said, “I testify that you are my Imam before Allah. Al-Rida (a.s.) wept and said, “O uncle, did not hear my father say, “The Messenger of Allah has said, “May Allah take my souls and the souls of my father in service for the cause of the son of the best slave girl, the son of al-Nawbiya (a town in Sudan) lady with a fresh smelling mouth, the lady of who will give birth to a purified one. May Allah condemn the ’U‘aybiss (the ‘Abbassides) and their descendents, the mischief makers who murder them (the Imams) for years, months and days, cause them huge sufferings and cause them to endure bitter frustrations. He (abu Ja‘far (a.s.) he live exiled, away from home and suffering the pain of the murder of his father and grandfather. One who is has disappeared (from the eyes of his loved ones). About whom it will be said, “His is dead or perished. No one will in which valleys he will travel. Can such a person, O uncle, be anyone other than my own son?” I then said, “You have spoken the truth, may Allah take my souls in service for your cause.”
